verdict.rationale: Linear's own agent docs describe OAuth app scopes for agents, such as app:assignable and app:mentionable, and the API supports OAuth2 alongside personal API keys. That shows agents get app-specific credentials with scoped permissions, but the evidence never shows fine-grained read/write data scopes or least-privilege restrictions on keys. Missing for 10: documented read/write or resource-level scope options, scope restriction for personal API keys, team-limited credential scoping, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: app:assignable | Allow the app to be assigned as a delegate on issues and made a member of projects app:mentionable | Allow the app to be mentioned in issues, documents, and other editor surfaces
The Linear API supports personal API keys and OAuth2 authentication.
Linear supports OAuth2 authentication, which is recommended if you're building applications to integrate with Linear.
